Let

\[
f(x)=\frac{1}{(1+2^{\sin x})(1+2^{\cos x})}.
\]

Since \(\sin x\) and \(\cos x\) are \(2\pi\)-periodic, \(f\) is \(2\pi\)-periodic.

First note the identity

\[
f(x)+f\left(x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)+f(x+\pi)+f\left(x+\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)=1.
\]

Indeed, writing \(s=\sin x\), \(c=\cos x\),

\[
f(x)=\frac{1}{(1+2^s)(1+2^c)},
\]

\[
f\left(x+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{2^s}{(1+2^s)(1+2^c)},
\]

\[
f(x+\pi)=\frac{2^{s+c}}{(1+2^s)(1+2^c)},
\]

\[
f\left(x+\frac{3\pi}{2}\right)=\frac{2^c}{(1+2^s)(1+2^c)}.
\]

Adding gives

\[
\frac{1+2^s+2^{s+c}+2^c}{(1+2^s)(1+2^c)}=1.
\]

Therefore, over any full period,

\[
\int_a^{a+2\pi} f(x)\,dx
=
\int_0^{\pi/2}\left[f(a+t)+f(a+t+\pi/2)+f(a+t+\pi)+f(a+t+3\pi/2)\right]dt
=
\frac{\pi}{2}.
\]

Now

\[
\frac{53\pi}{4}-\frac{25\pi}{4}=7\pi=3(2\pi)+\pi.
\]

Since

\[
\frac{25\pi}{4}=6\pi+\frac{\pi}{4},
\]

the integral is

\[
3\cdot \frac{\pi}{2}+\int_{\pi/4}^{5\pi/4} f(x)\,dx.
\]

It remains to evaluate

\[
R=\int_{\pi/4}^{5\pi/4} f(x)\,dx.
\]

Split at \(3\pi/4\):

\[
R=\int_0^{\pi/2}\left[f\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+t\right)+f\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}+t\right)\right]dt.
\]

Let

\[
A=\frac{\sin t+\cos t}{\sqrt2},\qquad B=\frac{\cos t-\sin t}{\sqrt2}.
\]

Then

\[
\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+t\right)=A,\qquad \cos\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+t\right)=B,
\]

and

\[
\sin\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}+t\right)=B,\qquad \cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}+t\right)=-A.
\]

Thus

\[
f\left(\frac{\pi}{4}+t\right)+f\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}+t\right)
=
\frac{1}{(1+2^A)(1+2^B)}
+
\frac{1}{(1+2^B)(1+2^{-A})}.
\]

Since \(\frac{1}{1+2^{-A}}=\frac{2^A}{1+2^A}\), this becomes

\[
\frac{1+2^A}{(1+2^A)(1+2^B)}=\frac{1}{1+2^B}.
\]

So

\[
R=\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{1}{1+2^B}\,dt,
\qquad
B=\frac{\cos t-\sin t}{\sqrt2}.
\]

But

\[
B\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-t\right)=-B(t).
\]

Therefore,

\[
\frac{1}{1+2^{B(t)}}+\frac{1}{1+2^{B(\pi/2-t)}}=1.
\]

Hence

\[
R=\frac12\cdot \frac{\pi}{2}=\frac{\pi}{4}.
\]

Finally,

\[
\int_{25\pi/4}^{53\pi/4}\frac{1}{(1+2^{\sin x})(1+2^{\cos x})}\,dx
=
3\cdot \frac{\pi}{2}+\frac{\pi}{4}
=
\frac{7\pi}{4}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{7\pi}{4}}
\]

27B·v4.method: Four-shift identity gives full-period integral; decompose 7π; prove residual half-period via partitioning and t→π/2−t symmetry.
